hypothesis: The user (31 Oct 2026): 'in the EM step we do not need noisy observations to get the kernel; once we have the kernel we use BP on the noisy sequence.' With clean sequences nothing is hidden, so EM collapses to ordinary maximum likelihood of the transitions, max_theta sum_{n,k} log K_theta(a_{k+1} | a_k), and BP is needed only at use time, to turn the learned kernel and a noisy sequence into E[a | x] and the score at any noise level. This is exactly the diffusion setting (score networks train on clean data), so it is the same-information comparison: Marc's July remark ('no noising is needed to identify the prior') tested against the networks. E34 measured the clean-versus-noisy gap on Allen-Cahn for E33's kernel arms (clean 1.6-3x better for the tilted spline and the MDN) but never with the neural energy kernel, never on the Laplace chain, never against networks trained on the same clean data, and never with more than 2048 sequences. E58 does all four, on small and large data.
design: CHAINS. (i) The Laplace chain on E03's bundles (e03._cell_common, tags exp31-*), seeds 0-15, so every row pairs with E03's frozen networks, E30's mixture and MDN and E56's noisy-EM kernels. (ii) The Allen-Cahn field on E33's bundles (e33._common, tags e33-*), cells T0.3_h1_L32 (cold, domains) and T1_iso_L32 (warm), seeds 0-7, pairing with E33's kernels and oracles, E54's CNN and E55. SIZES N in (32, 128, 512, 2048, 8192, 32768) training sequences on both chains. FIT. Clean training chains -> the transition histogram Xi on the 401-point grid (em.clean_statistics, linear interpolation, the t -> 0 limit of the E-step) -> repeated M-steps of the SAME kernel code E56 uses, so clean and noisy fits differ only in Xi; checkpoints on E55's EM_LADDER (10 ... 2400); selected on the validation bundle's pooled BP risk (the rule of every learned arm, networks included); the held-out clean log-likelihood per transition on clean validation chains recorded at every checkpoint (the oracle-free alternative and the step-efficiency curve). KERNEL ARMS: energy_h16 (the headline; E56's screen winner), energy_h32, energy_h64 (capacity): markov_score.energy_kernel.NeuralEnergyKernel, uniform start, lr 1e-2, 10 Adam steps per M-step with step halving; the ideal family: laplace_clean (LaplaceAR1Kernel, exact M-step) on the Laplace chain, pair_clean (E33's site energy, PairEnergyKernel) on the field; mixture_clean (the thesis kernel, C = 8). BP at use: grid BP with the learned kernel; initial law the standard normal on the Laplace chain (as E03/E56) and the kernel's own invariant law on the field (as E33/E34). NETWORK ARMS, trained in E58 at EVERY size on both chains under ONE recipe (E03's: standard DSM on the clean chains, per-example level from the twelve, fresh noise every step, batch 64, Adam, 32k steps on the checkpoint ladder, validation selection): global MLP (hidden 128 x 128) and window CNN (radius 4, width 64), E03's screened configurations. E03's frozen MLP and window rows at N <= 2048 on the Laplace chain are a reproduction check of E58's own. LINEAR FLOOR (lmmse) from each chain's exact covariance on the same test bundle; on the field it also gates the pairing against E33's lmmse_true. ESTIMAND: the pooled relative score error over the test bundle's chains, sites and twelve levels (e14._pooled = e03._risk on region all). BUDGET: fixed from the laptop timing of 31 Oct before any run (clean Xi 5 ms at N = 2048; one energy M-step 0.43 s at width 16 and 1.43 s at width 64; it does not depend on N): no timing part; ladder to 2400 and 32k network steps as registered.

predeclared_predictions.P1: Laplace chain, the same-information fight. energy_h16 has a lower seed-mean risk than E58's global MLP and than E58's window CNN at every N in (32, 128, 512, 2048, 8192, 32768), and is lower in at least 13 of 16 paired seeds against each, at each N.
predeclared_predictions.P2: Laplace chain, the price of learning through noise. energy_h16 (clean) has a lower seed-mean risk than E56's energy arm (noisy EM, same width, same bundles) at every N in (32, 128, 512, 2048), lower in at least 13 of 16 paired seeds.
predeclared_predictions.P3: Laplace chain, against the strongest network. At N in (512, 2048) energy_h16 has a lower seed-mean risk than the best of E03's six frozen networks at that N, lower in at least 13 of 16 paired seeds.
predeclared_predictions.P4: Allen-Cahn, the same-information fight. On both cells, energy_h16 has a lower seed-mean risk than E58's global MLP and window CNN at every N, lower in at least 7 of 8 paired seeds against each.
predeclared_predictions.P5: Allen-Cahn, the right family. On both cells at N in (32, 128, 512, 2048), pair_clean (the five-parameter site energy) has a lower seed-mean risk than energy_h16, lower in at least 7 of 8 paired seeds.
predeclared_predictions.P6: Data efficiency. energy_h16 at N = 128 has a lower seed-mean risk than the window CNN at N = 32768, on the Laplace chain and on the cold field cell T0.3_h1_L32.

descriptive.D1: Small and large data: every arm's seed-mean risk against N from 32 to 32768 on both chains, and the local slopes; do the networks catch up with the kernel as N grows?
descriptive.D2: Capacity with clean data: energy_h16 against energy_h32 and energy_h64 per N (overfitting at small N?).
descriptive.D3: The clean-to-noisy ratio per N: Laplace against E56's noisy energy arm; Allen-Cahn against E55's energy kernel when it is frozen.
descriptive.D4: Step efficiency: held-out clean log-likelihood and validation risk against M-steps for the kernels, validation risk against SGD steps for the networks.
descriptive.D5: Cost: seconds per M-step and per network step, and total training time, per arm and N.
descriptive.D6: The ideal families (laplace_clean, pair_clean) and the thesis kernel (mixture_clean) for reference.

predeclared_analysis: tools/core/read_e58.py, written with tests/test_read_e58.py in BOTH directions on made-up tables before any confirmatory row exists (a failed or missing fit counts AGAINST every prediction it enters; a seed mean needs every seed; a paired win needs both rows). Gates: G1 Laplace, E58's sq_ref per (seed, N <= 2048, t) equals E30's within relative 1e-12 (E56's gate); G1 field, E58's lmmse risk per (cell, seed) equals E33's lmmse_true within relative 1e-10; G2, the reproduction check: E58's MLP and window seed means at N <= 2048 within 10% of E03's frozen ones (reported, a failure flags the network arms); G3, at the cap read from the selected checkpoint (>= 2400 for kernels, the last step for networks) and reported as an upper bound where more than half the seeds are capped.
